events.title: Uncomputable Thread
about: Uncomputable Thread is a presentation, conversation and participatory movement workshop by artist Taeyoon Choi, created in collaboration with scholar Alexander R. Galloway, choreographer Cori Kresge and artist Roopa Vasudevan. The work examines the history of textile in relation to computing, alongside the artistic and political significance of what cannot be computed and draws on themes of the current exhibition, Technologies of Relation, which includes works by both Choi and Vasudevan.

Choi and Galloway’s presentation weaves together their long collaboration and ongoing conversation about the aesthetics and politics of code and textile, followed by a discussion moderated by Vasudevan. Kresge directs a participatory movement workshop that extends the conversation toward visceral and communal experience. Together, the project explores uncomputability as a creative framework for thinking about contemporary technologies and social systems, connecting the threads of cotton and fiber-optic cables running through data centers.

최태윤 Taeyoon Choi is an artist, writer, and educator who explores the poetics of technology and human relations, working with images, text, and code in collaboration with fellow artists and community members. In 2013, he co-founded the School for Poetic Computation, a hybrid school, residency, and research group exploring the intersections of code, design, hardware, and theory. His work has been presented at institutions including the Whitney Museum of American Art and MASS MoCA.

Cori Kresge is a New York-based dance artist whose practice moves across choreography, somatic inquiry, participatory structures, and poetry. Her work has been presented by Goethe in the Skyways, Elevation 1049, Beach Sessions Rockaway, Green Space, and Dance Roulette, among others. A certified teacher and stager for the Merce Cunningham Trust, she is also the author of two chapbooks, isn’t devotion (2019) and Combustion Suite (2023), and the founder of Alexander R. Galloway is a writer and computer programmer working on issues in philosophy, technology, and theories of mediation, and Professor of Media, Culture, and Communication at New York University. He is the author of several books on digital media and critical theory, including The Interface Effect (Polity, 2012). events.title: Artist Tour
about: Join Exhibiting Artist Jimena Sarno for a special public tour of the exhibition Rhapsody.

The artist will guide visitors through the exhibition’s three major installations: Rhapsody, which brings together weaving, film, sound, and sculpture through collaborations with artists and makers from the Global South; Las Tres Gracias, an operatic installation exploring the Western myth of democracy and cycles of destruction and renewal; and Life in the Forest, a film, sound, and sculpture installation examining the normalization of contemporary forms of fascism.

In Rhapsody, Jimena Sarno engages craft traditions to imagine a future built on values of collectivity, reconfiguration, and repair. Within a global context of extreme violence, fragmentation, and destruction, the artists share time, space, and resources through making and the collective production of alternative forms of knowledge. The central installation features objects made using techniques—including weaving, woodworking, and ceramics—that rely on knowledge passed from maker to maker. These objects are tools, at once utilitarian and utopian, designed for a hoped-for, not-so-distant future built on solidarity and mutual care.
Learn more about the exhibition and artist here.
Please meet in the lobby at the map model upon arrival. Space is limited and registration is required.
Support for Rhapsody is provided by The Coby Foundation, Ltd. In-kind support has been provided by Local Industries.
Installation view of Jimena Sarno: Rhapsody as installed at MASS MoCA, North Adams, MA. Photo: Jon Verney courtesy of MASS MoCA.

events.title: Endea Owens & The Cookout
about: Known as one of jazz’s most vibrant emerging artists, Endea Owens is a Detroit-raised recording artist, bassist, and composer. She has been mentored by jazz icons the likes of Marcus Belgrave, Rodney Whitaker, and Ron Carter. She has toured and performed with Wynton Marsalis, Jennifer Holliday, Diana Ross, Rhonda Ross, Solange, Jon Batiste, Jazzmeia Horn, Dee Dee Bridgewater, and Cyrus Chestnut, to name a few.

In 2018, Owens graduated from The Juilliard School, and joined the Late Show with Stephen Colbert as a member of the house band, Stay Human, where she remained through Colbert’s final season. Since then, Owens has won an Emmy, Grammy, and a George Foster Peabody Award. Owens’ work has appeared on Jon Batiste’s Grammy Award-winning album We Are, Oscar-nominated film Judas and the Black Messiah, and H.E.R.’s widely acclaimed Super Bowl LV performance.

In 2022, Owens composed an original piece about the life of Ida B. Wells entitled “Ida’s Crusade” for the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra’s National Youth Orchestra which was also performed by the NYO Carnegie Hall Orchestra. Owens has written for brands such as Pyer Moss and Glossier. She was the curator for the National Arts Club and also a fellow for “Jazz is: Now!” with the National Jazz Museum in Harlem, where she presented original compositions, curated series, and headlined performances for the 2022–2023 season. Owens released her debut album Feel Good Music in 2023.
This performance is supported by Terry Spaeth and Wendy Shannon-Spaeth.

events.title: On the Calculation of Volume (Book I) by Solvej Balle
about: “How on earth did this book come into being? It’s like it has always been here in this world with us, like one feels about the best art. I am torn as I read it between lingering and racing ahead, and I think about my days completely differently now.” — Sheila Heti Lizzie Whitman convenes this casual book club around Solvej Balle’s utterly riveting On the Calculation of Volume (Book I) — the grand opening of her speculative fiction septology, winner of the 2022 Nordic Council Literature Prize (Scandinavia’s most important literary award) for being “a masterpiece of its time.” Balle was also nominated for the International Booker Prize and a National Book Award for this book.

Tara Selter, the heroine of On the Calculation of Volume, has involuntarily stepped off the train of time: in her world, November 18 repeats itself endlessly. We meet Tara on her 122nd November 18: she no longer experiences the changes of days, weeks, months, or seasons. She finds herself in a lonely new reality without being able to explain why: how is it that she wakes every morning on the same exact day, knowing to the exact second when the blackbird will burst into song and when the rain will begin? Will she ever be able to share her new life with her beloved and now chronically befuddled husband? And on top of her profound isolation and confusion, Tara takes in with pain how slight a difference she makes in the world. And as she puts it: “That’s how little the activities of one person matter on the eighteenth of November.”
Balle is hypnotic and masterful in her remixing of the endless recursive day, creating curious little folds of time and foreshadowings: her flashbacks light up inside the text like old flash bulbs.
Can’t make the event? Order On the Calculation of Volume here.

Lizzie Whitman is a local educator, reader, and book club enthusiast. With an education in the Great Books Program and linguistics, she has been asking the question, “What are you reading right now?” for decades.
Core support for the Department of Public Programs is provided by the WLS Spencer Foundation.

events.title: Last Week in End Times Cinema & Algorithm of the Night
about: “A. S. Hamrah’s writing on film is a delight... Like all the best criticism, his writing makes art and life feel less lonely.” —Elif Batuman A.S. Hamrah is single-handedly re-inventing film criticism with a unique archive of unfortunate movie bulletins published in the best indie print journals and magazines, and compiled for his beloved weekly newsletter. His two most recent books, Last Week in End Times Cinema (Semiotext(e)) and Algorithm of the Night (n+1) are R&D Store best-sellers. Join Hamrah for a conversation about film, filmmakers, critical writing, and the state of movies in 2026.
Can’t make the event? Order A. S. Hamrah’s books here, and we’ll get them signed for you.

A.S. Hamrah is a film critic and writer. He is the author of Algorithm of the Night: Film Writing 2019-2025 (Semiotext(e)) and Last Week in End Times Cinema (n+1). He writes for a variety of publications, including The New York Review of Books, Bookforum, Fast Company, n+1, The Nation, and The Criterion Collection. From 2008 to 2016, he worked as a brand and trend analyst for the television industry, and he produced a documentary feature which was the opening-night film at the Museum of Modern Art’s Doc Fortnight 2022. In addition, he has worked as a political pollster, a football cinematographer, and for the director Raúl Ruiz. He lives in New York.

events.title: Mirrored Pool
events.detail: Tom Lee, Lisa Kaplan and Matthew Duvall
about: Where do we fit in this endless universe? Glimpse the precious fragility of our life on Planet Earth as we peer into the Mirrored Pool.

Mirrored Pool is a puppetry and music collaboration between acclaimed puppeteer and La MaMa resident artist Tom Lee and musicians Lisa Kaplan and Matthew Duvall of the Grammy-award winning sextet Eighth Blackbird. The piece explores humanity’s place in our vast universe, showcasing the virtuosity of Eighth Blackbird’s music against the vital, human power of puppetry. Mirrored Pool takes special inspiration from astronomer Carl Sagan, whose work on the Voyager spacecrafts and the Golden Record are now the most distant human-made objects and sounds from our planet — currently 15.7 billion miles away from Earth.

Created and performed by Tom Lee, Lisa Kaplan, and Matthew Duvall Puppets & masks by Jaerin Son Additional puppet design by Averly Sheltraw Lighting by Seojung Jang Puppetry direction by Justin Perkins An Eighth Blackbird production in association with Yara Arts Group with support from the MAP Fund.
Specialty sponsorship for MASS MoCA’s winter theater productions provided by J.H. Maxymillian, Inc.
Mirrored Pool. Photo courtesy of the artist.

events.title: Kimberly Bartosik: bLUr
about: bLUr, choreographed by Kimberly Bartosik, is a highly physical and emotionally intense dance piece in which five performers navigate scenes of desire, care, violence, and tender rescue.

Exploring the haunting impact of witnessing a loved one’s overdose, but moving beyond explicit narratives of the opioid crisis, the work uses visceral movement cycles to embody the violent cravings and internal battles of substance abuse. Built out of Bartosik’s own experiences and deeply shaped by the individuality of her performers, bLUr is both personal and universal as it warps time and reminds us of our fragility, power, and need for one another.

Kimberly Bartosik is a choreographer, performer, educator, and writer. As a member of the Merce Cunningham Dance Company for nine years, Bartosik received a Bessie Award for Exceptional Artistry. She is currently an Advisor for The Ailey School/Fordham BFA Program and teaches at SUNY/Purchase and the Merce Cunningham Trust.

She is a 2024 National Dance Project Production Grant (NDP) recipient from the New England Foundation for the Arts; a 2025 New York State Council on the Arts/NYSCA Support for Artists Award grantee with support of the Office of the Governor and the New York State Legislature; and a 2025 Harkness Foundation for Dance Project Grant recipient, among numerous other awards. Bartosik’s work has been commissioned and presented by BAM Next Wave, New York Live Arts, Crossing the Line Festival, Bates Dance Festival, Torn Space Theater, American Dance Festival, LUMBERYARD, American Realness, Abrons Art Center, Gibney, Danspace Project, The Kitchen, La Mama, and others. She has toured to Supersense: Festival of the Ecstatic (Melbourne, Australia), Bratislava in Movement (Slovakia), Wexner Arts Center, Dance Place, American Dance Festival, The Yard, MASS MoCA/Jacob’s Pillow, Flynn Space, Bates Dance Festival, Columbia College, Centre Chorégraphique National de Franche-Comté à Belfort, Festival Rencontres chorégraphique internationales de Seine-Saint Denis, Artdanthe Festival, Church, Mount Tremper Arts, and others.
This program is supported in part by the Irene Hunter Fund for Dance at MASS MoCA in association with Jacob’s Pillow.

events.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
about: A decade after his death, genre-defying filmmaker William Greaves has one last trick up his sleeve with what he considered the most important event he captured on film: a 1972 party he engineered with the living luminaries of the Harlem Renaissance.

For four hours, this extraordinary group—many of whom had not seen each other in fifty years—reminisced, critiqued, argued, laughed and drank while wrestling with their place in a rapidly shifting cultural landscape.

Shot on 16mm film, newly restored and now directed by Greaves’ son David, this landmark film is at once a self-exploration and an inquiry into the heart of the critical mass of energy called the Harlem Renaissance.

William Greaves’ intent was not only to document these artists and intellectuals as they spoke about their lives and work but also to plumb the meaning of the extraordinary creative period in which they lived to help us better understand how culture has been passed on from one generation to another and the role that the artist plays in keeping it alive.

“The movie flows beautifully, with a seamless mix of found and originally shot material... The past comes vibrantly alive in these rooms, but always circles back to the present and often points to the future.” Manohla Dargis. A New York Times Critic's Pick!
Directed by David Greaves, Liani Greaves, William Greaves · PG-13

events.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
about: Harry Lehman (John Turturro) is an aging pickpocket who plies his trade with ever-diminishing returns in a drastically changed New York.
Wallets stuffed with cash have been replaced by easily canceled credit cards, and Harry struggles to make ends meet as he cares for his disabled wife, Rosie.
When he unwittingly purloins and fences a valuable USB stick, Harry finds himself in a race against time to return the loot or face the rage of a vengeful crime family.

“THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is remarkable in many ways, first among them Turturro’s performance. Somehow, despite a 40-year career full of memorable roles, Turturro is still underrated. This movie lets him showcase all of his best qualities; he gets to be quick-witted and fleet-footed, but also full of love and grief.” Alissa Wilkinson. A New York Times Critic's Pick!
Directed by Noah Segan · R

events.title: Wicker
about: An audacious comedic fable about sex, marriage, and the absurdities of social convention, WICKER tells the wholly original love story of an ostracized fisherwoman (Olivia Colman) who commissions a husband to be made by the local basketmaker (Peter Dinklage).

When her wicker husband (Alexander Skarsgård) proves more spectacular than she ever imagined, his soulful spirit and unique prowess awaken something inside her, setting off a wave of jealousy, fascination, and upheaval that threatens the very fabric of village life.

“Bouncing all the way to a truly perfect ending, WICKER is funny and freaky and sweetly romantic. It is also relentless in its conviction that the most destabilizing force in a society is a woman who dares to ask for what she wants.”Jeannette Catsoulis. A New York Times Critic's Pick!
Directed by Alex Huston Fischer, Eleanor Wilson · R

events.title: Wild Horse Nine
about: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are dispatched from Santiago to Easter island by their bureau chief, MJ (Steve Buscemi).

Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students (Mariana di Girolamo and Ailín Salas) threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.
WILD HORSE NINE is the new film from writer/director Martin McDonagh (THE BANSHEES OF INISHERIN, IN BRUGES).

“Elegiac and delightfully foul-mouthed, the film is both a political thriller and a meditation on the nature of legacy, memory and what makes life worth living, anchored by a career-best performance from Malkovich, who is never better than when he’s playing a villainous but lovable rascal”
“A bittersweet hangout film about lonely, crumpled men facing up to mortality, dealing with the consequences of violence and chewing the fat to outlandishly funny effect.”
Directed by Martin McDonagh · R

“Bouncing all the way to a truly perfect ending, WICKER is funny and freaky and sweetly romantic. It is also relentless in its conviction that the most destabilizing force in a society is a woman who dares to ask for what she wants.”Jeannette Catsoulis. A New York Times Critic's Pick!
Directed by Alex Huston Fischer, Eleanor Wilson · R

events.title: Wild Horse Nine
about: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are dispatched from Santiago to Easter island by their bureau chief, MJ (Steve Buscemi).

Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students (Mariana di Girolamo and Ailín Salas) threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.
WILD HORSE NINE is the new film from writer/director Martin McDonagh (THE BANSHEES OF INISHERIN, IN BRUGES).

“Elegiac and delightfully foul-mouthed, the film is both a political thriller and a meditation on the nature of legacy, memory and what makes life worth living, anchored by a career-best performance from Malkovich, who is never better than when he’s playing a villainous but lovable rascal”
“A bittersweet hangout film about lonely, crumpled men facing up to mortality, dealing with the consequences of violence and chewing the fat to outlandishly funny effect.”
Directed by Martin McDonagh · R

events.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
about: Harry Lehman (John Turturro) is an aging pickpocket who plies his trade with ever-diminishing returns in a drastically changed New York.
Wallets stuffed with cash have been replaced by easily canceled credit cards, and Harry struggles to make ends meet as he cares for his disabled wife, Rosie.
When he unwittingly purloins and fences a valuable USB stick, Harry finds himself in a race against time to return the loot or face the rage of a vengeful crime family.

events.title: Fatherland
about: Opens Friday 11/20.

At the height of the Cold War, the writer Thomas Mann and his daughter—actress, writer, and rally driver—Erika embark on a road trip in a black Buick cruiser across a divided Germany in ruins, traveling from the Allied-occupied city of Frankfurt to Soviet-controlled Weimar.
The new film from director Paweł Pawlikowski (IDA, COLD WAR) stars Sandra Hüller (ANATOMY OF A FALL) and Hanns Zischler (MUNICH).
“A film of deep, luminous feeling... Huller’s ability to let you into her characters’ thinking is a marvel.” Manohla Dargis. A New York Times Critic's Pick!
Directed by Paweł Pawlikowski · NR

events.title: The Devil Queen
about: Rio de Janeiro’s criminal underworld is run by an unexpected boss: Diaba (Milton Gonçalves), a femme queen with a taste for power and violence. When the police come after her boy toy, Diaba attempts to find a scapegoat to take the blame, and a plot to dethrone Her Majesty arises.

Always clad in gloriously colorful outfits and accessories inspired by Afro-Brazilian culture, Diaba runs a mob of eccentric misfits made up of drag queens, pimps, prostitutes, and queer folks of all stripes. The movie’s bold and audacious color palette and camp aesthetic evokes the early films of Pedro Almodóvar, while its stylized and over-the-top violence is giving Quentin Tarantino queer fever dream.
Directed by Antônio Carlos da Fontoura · NR

events.title: Killer of Sheep
about: Join us for a free screening of KILLER OF SHEEP as part of our 20th Anniversary Kickoff, presenting three films from Amherst Cinema's first year. Free tickets are available the day of the celebration on a first come, first served basis. Arrive early for treats and games!
KILLER OF SHEEP originally played at Amherst Cinema on October 25, 2007, with director Charles Burnett in person.
In the Los Angeles neighborhood of Watts, Stan, employed at a slaughterhouse, is suffering from the emotional side effects of his bloody occupation to such a degree that his entire life unhinges.

One of the crown jewels of the Black indie filmmaking movement known as the L.A. Rebellion, KILLER OF SHEEP focuses on everyday life in Black communities in a manner rarely seen in American cinema—combining lyrical elements with a starkly neorealist, documentary-style approach that chronicles the unfolding story with depth and riveting simplicity.

The film has been declared a national treasure by the Library of Congress and was among the first 50 films placed on the National Film Registry. In 2022, it was named the 43rd greatest film of all time on the British Film Institute Sight and Sound poll.
KILLER OF SHEEP is presented in a new 4K restoration.

“Shot in Watts in the early ’70s and completed in 1977, the film was Mr. Burnett’s M.F.A. thesis project and never meant for a commercial release. He operated the 16-millimeter camera himself, edited the black-and-white images into a visual poem and added the ballads, the jazz and the moody blues that seep into your head like smoke. The result is an American masterpiece, independent to the bone.” Manohla Dargis. A New York Times Critic's Pick!
Directed by Charles Burnett · NR

events.title: Little Miss Sunshine
about: Join us for a free screening of LITTLE MISS SUNSHINE as part of our 20th Anniversary Kickoff, presenting three films from Amherst Cinema's first year. Free tickets are available the day of the celebration on a first come, first served basis. Arrive early for treats and games!
LITTLE MISS SUNSHINE originally played at Amherst Cinema in December of 2006.
Father Richard (Greg Kinnear) is desperately trying to sell his motivational success program... with no success.
Meanwhile, “pro-honesty” mom Sheryl (Toni Collette) lends support to her eccentric family, including her depressed brother (Steve Carell), fresh out of the hospital after being jilted by his lover.
Then there are the younger Hoovers—the seven-year-old, would-be beauty queen Olive (Abigail Breslin) and Dwayne (Paul Dano), a Nietzsche-reading teen who has taken a vow of silence.
Topping off the family is the foul-mouthed grandfather (Alan Arkin), whose outrageous behavior recently got him evicted from his retirement home.
When Olive is invited to compete in the “Little Miss Sunshine” pageant in far-off California, the family piles into their rusted-out VW bus to rally behind her—with riotously funny results.
LITTLE MISS SUNSHINE is presented in a new 4K restoration.
“Harks back to the anti-establishment, countercultural comedies of the 1970s... You just won’t see a better acted, and better cast, movie than LITTLE MISS SUNSHINE.” –Roger Ebert
Directed by Jonathan Dayton, Valerie Faris · R

events.title: Pan's Labyrinth
about: Join us for a free screening of PAN'S LABYINRTH as part of our 20th Anniversary Kickoff, presenting three films from Amherst Cinema's first year. Free tickets are available the day of the celebration on a first come, first served basis. Arrive early for treats and games!
PAN'S LABYRINTH originally played at Amherst Cinema January through March of 2007.
An Academy Award–winning dark fable set five years after the end of the Spanish Civil War, PAN'S LABYRINTH encapsulates the rich visual style and genre-defying craft of Guillermo del Toro.

Eleven-year-old Ofelia (Ivana Baquero, in a mature and tender performance) comes face to face with the horrors of fascism when she and her pregnant mother are uprooted to the countryside, where her new stepfather (Sergi López), a sadistic captain in General Francisco Franco’s army, hunts down Republican guerrillas refusing to give up the fight.

The violent reality in which Ofelia lives merges seamlessly with her fantastical interior world when she meets a faun in a decaying labyrinth and is set on a strange, mythic journey that is at once terrifying and beautiful.
In his revisiting of this bloody period in Spanish history, del Toro creates a vivid depiction of the monstrosities of war infiltrating a child’s imagination and threatening the innocence of youth.
PAN'S LABYRINTH is presented in a new 4K restoration.
“One of the greatest of all fantasy films.” –Roger Ebert
Directed by Guillermo del Toro · R

events.title: The Exquisite Hour, Part 2
about: This screening is free to the general public. Tickets are available only at the Amherst Cinema box office on a first-come, first-served basis. They can be picked up in advance during the Cinema’s regular box office hours, or at the door the evening of the screening.
Following an inaugural program in February 2026, this screening features a set of 16mm experimental films that harness the beauties and intensities of photochemical filmmaking.

“The Exquisite Hour” takes its name from a film originally completed by Phil Solomon in 1989, which was intended, in part, as a rumination on the impending death of celluloid film. Nearly forty years later, the filmic medium is still alive due in no small measure to an experimental film tradition that has been expanding the aesthetic capacities of photochemical filmmaking for decades.

The second edition of “The Exquisite Hour” showcases six contributions to this tradition that were created by artists from different generations and locales. While these works employ varied formats, techniques, and methodologies, they all share an investment in the future of analog film culture, which this program seeks to affirm and extend.
Films will be projected from a mix of 16mm and digital.
Curated by Abraham Ravett, Professor of Film and Photography, Hampshire College, and Josh Guilford, Assistant Professor of English in Film and Media Studies, Amherst College.
Presented in partnership with the English Department and Film and Media Studies Program at Amherst College.

Magdalena Bermudez, 2025, 16mm on digital, b&w, sound, 12 min “Women pretend to be rocks. Military operations masquerade as art education. One woman deserts to pursue a more radical act of unselfing.” –Magdalena Bermudez Ericka Beckman, 2002, 16mm, color, sound, 10 min “Switch Center is a tribute to the futuristic architecture of the Soviet post war period, and a reaction to seeing it transitioned to shopping malls or global corporate office structures. I was invited by Balazs Bela Studio in Budapest to produce a short experimental film in Hungary. I was the first American artist to be invited by this famous film collective after the fall of Soviet power. The collaboration took place in August 2000, culminating in Switch Center, a ten minute experimental documentary shot in many defunct Danube Water Works locations on the outskirts of Budapest. The architecture of a 1960's water…
Directed by various

events.title: Elsinore
about: Andrew Scott delivers his strongest performance honoring the real-life story of Ian Charleson, the CHARIOTS OF FIRE actor who courageously pushed through AIDS to play Hamlet at London’s National Theatre.
Facing his own mortality with unflinching honesty, wit, and grace, Charleson delivers a courageous performance that becomes a source of healing and inspiration for those around him.
Directed by Simon Stone · R

events.title: The Beastmaster
about: Calling all dungeon masters! The follow-up to PHANTASM from young filmmaker Don Coscarelli, THE BEASTMASTER is a sublime thrill-ride in the 1980s sword-and-sorcery sweepstakes. It's also the only one that was photographed by John Alcott, the Oscar-winning, Kubrick favorite DP who filmed THE SHINING and A CLOCKWORK ORANGE.

Dar (Marc Singer) is the crown prince of a family that was slaughtered by a lords of evil. When he grows to manhood, Dar cultivates the ability to communicate with animals and seeks revenge on the monstrous priest known as Maax (Rip Torn).
Like CONAN THE BARBARIAN and KRULL, THE BEASTMASTER is an over-the-top mix of fantasy, action, and horror that could only have been birthed in the 1980s.
Directed by Don Coscarelli · PG

events.title: NT Live: Golden Boy
about: Josh O’Connor (The Crown; CHALLENGERS) leads the cast in this searing revival of Clifford Odets’ knockout American classic.

1930s New York, at the height of the Depression. Joe Bonaparte is a gifted young violinist with a future in music, until a chance at fame and fortune lures him into the brutal world of professional boxing. He must confront what he’s willing to sacrifice, who he’s willing to become and how to find his place in a world that demands he choose a side.

Brought to life with a live string quartet and filmed live from the Almeida Theatre. Olivier Award-winner Sam Yates (NT Live: Vanya) directs this propulsive drama exploring ambition, identity, and the high price of success.
Runtime includes a 15-minute intermission.
Directed by Sam Yates · NR

events.title: Emerging Filmmakers of Western Massachusetts 2026
about: This screening is free to the general public. Tickets are available only at the Amherst Cinema box office on a first-come, first-served basis. They can be picked up in advance during the Cinema’s regular box office hours, or at the door the evening of the screening.

The Easthampton Film Festival co-presents a lively selection of narrative and documentary shorts made by Western Massachusetts-based filmmakers, offering audiences an opportunity to experience stories rooted in places, people, and issues they know firsthand.

A panel of featured filmmakers joins us for a post-screening conversation led by Kt Baldassaro, Head of the Easthampton Film Festival Horror Film Subcommittee, Festival Moderator, and Public Ambassador.
Presented in partnership with the Easthampton Film Festival.
A man drives to Chicago to meet Frank, who doesn't answer his calls.
dir. Dinah Mack and Kate Way This documentary short tells the story of the restoration of the historic Holyoke Clock Tower.
Through a series of interactions within a liminal space, a man struggles to break free from the attention-grabbing devices of his companion.
dir. Lucas Fappiano and Colin Hodgson A short documentary about the re-opening of a beloved local live music venue and the lasting impact it continues to have on the community.

dir. Jordan Brooks and Brian Jones A lost man in a crumbling marriage discovers through a chance encounter that traveling back in time may actually be possible, he's faced with a choice: to change the past risking an uncertain future, or reclaim the path he's already on.
The youngest member of a combined family of nine navigates moving houses for the very first time. Presented in five chapters, documented by her older brothers over the course of a year.
This program is supported in part by a grant from the Amherst Cultural Council, a local agency which is supported by the Mass Cultural Council, a state agency.
Directed by various · NR

events.title: Joybubbles
about: Director Rachael J. Morrison, a Hampshire College alum, joins us for a post-film discussion.
This screening is free to Amherst Cinema Members.
JOYBUBBLES is a documentary about a boy who discovers he can control the global telephone system by whistling a magic tone.
Born blind and yearning for connection, his early obsession with the telephone sparks a subculture that shapes the future of hacking and technology.
An official selection of the 2026 Sundance Film Festival.
Please note that this film is presented with open audio description and open captions.
Bellwether is presented with support from Hotel UMass.
Directed by Rachael J. Morrison · NR

events.title: Tokyo Godfathers
about: In modern-day Tokyo, three homeless people’s lives are changed forever when they discover a baby girl at a garbage dump on Christmas Eve. As the New Year fast approaches, these three forgotten members of society band together to solve the mystery of the abandoned child and the fate of her parents. Along the way, encounters with seemingly unrelated events and people force them to confront their own haunted pasts, as they learn to face their future, together.
Join us for a holiday-adjacent animé from the director of PERFECT BLUE and PAPRIKA, co-written by Keiko Nobumoto (COWBOY BEBOP) and featuring a whimsical score by Keiichi Suzuki.
TOKYO GODFATHERS is a masterpiece by turns heartfelt, hilarious and highly original, a tale of hope and redemption in the face of seemingly insurmountable odds.
Directed by Satoshi Kon · PG-13

events.title: The Muppet Christmas Carol
about: Please note that passes cannot be redeemed for this screening.
The Muppets put their spin on the tale of Ebenezer Scrooge (Michael Caine), a Christmas-hating miser visited by three spirits.
They foretell his future and share secrets from his past and present, helping to change his view on life.
Brian Henson, the son of Muppet founder Jim Henson, took over directing duties after the untimely death of his father for THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL, a unique re-telling of the Charles Dickens tale.

The $5 Family Films series is supported in part by Greenfield Savings Bank and a grant from the Amherst Cultural Council, a local agency which is supported by the Mass Cultural Council, a state agency.

Different films will be appropriate for different children at different ages. We recommend Common Sense Media or the Parents Guide section of as helpful resources in determining what's right for your child.
Directed by Brian Henson · G

events.title: The Apartment
events.detail: Billy Wilder presented by Nina Kleinberg
about: Join us this fall for three films by Billy Wilder, featuring introductions by local film expert Nina Kleinberg.
For this final screening, Nina examines the visual style of the film and discusses how THE APARTMENT challenged the Hays Code.

In 1960, following the success of their collaboration on SOME LIKE IT HOT, director Billy Wilder reteamed with actor Jack Lemmon for what many consider the pinnacle of their respective careers: THE APARTMENT.

C.C. Bud Baxter (Lemmon) is a lowly Manhattan office drone with a lucrative sideline in renting out his apartment to adulterous company bosses and their mistresses. When Bud enters into a similar arrangement with the firm's personnel director, J.D. Sheldrake (Fred MacMurray), his career prospects begin to look up... and up. But when he discovers that Sheldrake's mistress is Fran Kubelik (Shirley MacLaine), the girl of his dreams, he finds himself forced to choose between his career and the woman he loves...
Winner of five Oscars, including Best Picture, THE APARTMENT features a wealth of Hollywood's finest talent on both sides of the camera at the top of their game.

About Nina Kleinberg: In the late 1960s, Nina attended film school at the University of Southern California. She then spent most of the 1970s working in the film industry in Los Angeles, mostly as an editor. Although she went on to a different career, she never gave up her love of film history and the film-making process.

Many of you know Nina from her appearances at Amherst Cinema, including her 2015 film series Film School in 90 Minutes, her 2016 series Out of this World on 1950s science fiction films, her 2019 series Print the Legend on classic Westerns, or her Science on Screen presentation on SINGIN' IN THE RAIN. Her seminar on CASABLANCA is a perpetual favorite with Amherst Cinema audiences, with many repeat viewers. In the fall of 2025, Nina introduced a popular series of three Pre-Code Classics.
Directed by Billy Wilder · NR

events.title: You Can See Everything
about: Thirty-four days before she's sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss.
Directed by Nathan Fielder, Lance Oppenheim · 2h 54m

events.title: Wild Horse Nine
about: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris and Lee are dispatched from Santiago to Easter Island by their bureau chief, MJ. Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.
Directed by Martin McDonagh · 1h 58m · R

events.title: Godzilla Minus Zero
about: War reduced Japan to zero, and Godzilla plunged it into minus. Two years have passed since then, and the country has faced agonizing struggles to achieve recovery and finally reclaim its daily life. Just as humanity managed to cling to a hard-won peace, a new threat strikes, crushing hope in an instant.
Directed by Takashi Yamazaki · 2h 15m

A young woman left her family for an unspecified reason. The husband determines to find out the truth and starts following his wife. At first, he suspects that a man is involved. But gradually, he finds out more and more strange behaviors and bizarre incidents that indicate something more than a possessed love affair.
Directed by Andrzej Żuławski · 2h 4m · R

events.title: Howl's Moving Castle (2004)
about: Young@Heart presents "Curl Up With a Good Film", a series highlighting classic films based on beloved children's books. This series is co-presented by the Milne Public Library. Sunday screenings will be presented in a sensory friendly environment with adjusted light and sound levels.
To ensure this presentation is as accessible to all-ages as possible, these screenings are presented with the English voice cast.

When Sophie, a shy young woman, is cursed with an old body by a spiteful witch, her only chance of breaking the spell lies with a self-indulgent yet insecure young wizard and his companions in his legged, walking castle.
Directed by Hayao Miyazaki · 1h 59m · PG

about: In 1949, German writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika embark on a road trip across a Germany in ruins, from US-dominated Frankfurt to Soviet-controlled Weimar.

events.title: Wild Horse Nine
about: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris and Lee are dispatched from Santiago to Easter Island by their bureau chief, MJ. Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.
Directed by Martin McDonagh · 1h 58m · R

events.title: Karaoke Night
about: Sing your heart out each and every Thursday starting at 8pm at the Images Cinema Lounge. No need to buy a ticket, just come by, sign up on the clipboard, and we take care of the rest. If you want to be the host for an upcoming karaoke, send an email to andrew@ Hosts get to introduce singers, encourage people to sign up for a song, and (if they want to) suggest a theme for the night.
The bartender will be available and ready to serve cocktails, beer, wine, and cider. The event is limited to people age 21 and over.
November 5: Paulette and Tania · November 12: Phil and Gwen · November 19: Allison Brandford
November 23: Mary 'Real Turkey' Redstone - SPECIAL WEDNESDAY NIGHT KARAOKE No Karaoke on Thanksgiving - Have a Happy Holiday!

events.title: Being Heumann
about: By special arrangement with the film team, we are presenting BEING HEUMANN with additional accessibility options.
All screenings will be presented with Open Captions.
On Sunday 11/29, all screenings will be Sensory Friendly with sound at a lower volume and the lights not all the way lowered.

On Wednesday 12/2, all screenings will be presented with Open Audio Description, with the descriptive audio track usually available via special devices being played live through the theater's speaker system.

Scrappy, defiant, and done being treated like a burden, Judy Heumann turns her outrage into a revolution. In 1977, she and more than 100 disability rights protestors send a very loud message: The system is broken—not us.
Directed by Sian Heder · 2h 7m · R

events.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
about: Harry Lehman is an aging pickpocket who plies his trade with ever-diminishing returns in a drastically changed New York. Wallets stuffed with cash have been replaced by easily cancelled credit cards, and Harry struggles to make ends meet as he cares for his disabled wife, Rosie. When he unwittingly purloins and fences a valuable USB stick, Harry finds himself in a race against time to return the loot or face the rage of a vengeful crime family.
Directed by Noah Segan · 1h 28m · R

events.title: Cultural Collab
about: The Williamstown Cultural District and Images Lounge present Cultural Collab, a monthly artist meetup on the last Monday of each month, 7 - 9pm. At each meetup three artists will briefly present their work, followed by conversation and social time. Hosted by artist Julie Henderson. Snacks will be provided; drinks will be available for purchase. No ticket needed.
If you are interested in presenting, email williamstownculturaldistrict@

Wallets stuffed with cash have been replaced by easily cancelled credit cards, and Harry struggles to make ends meet as he cares for his disabled wife, Rosie. When he unwittingly purloins and fences a valuable USB stick, Harry finds himself in a race against time to return the loot or face the rage of a vengeful crime family.
Directed by Noah Segan · 1h 28m · R

events.title: Being Heumann
about: By special arrangement with the film team, we are presenting BEING HEUMANN with additional accessibility options.
All screenings will be presented with Open Captions.
On Sunday 11/29, all screenings will be Sensory Friendly with sound at a lower volume and the lights not all the way lowered.

On Wednesday 12/2, all screenings will be presented with Open Audio Description, with the descriptive audio track usually available via special devices being played live through the theater's speaker system.

Scrappy, defiant, and done being treated like a burden, Judy Heumann turns her outrage into a revolution. In 1977, she and more than 100 disability rights protestors send a very loud message: The system is broken—not us.
Directed by Sian Heder · 2h 7m · R

events.title: Fjord
about: Following the deaths of Mihai's parents, Mihai and Lisbet Gheorghiu leave their life behind in Romania and move with their children to a remote village in Norway, hoping to rebuild their lives near Lisbet's family. But the fragile peace begins to unravel when the Gheorghiu family’s young daughter, Elia, arrives at school covered in bruises.
Directed by Cristian Mungiu · 2h 26m · R

events.title: Wicker
about: On the outskirts of a village by the sea, lives a Fisherwoman; smelly, single and perpetually ridiculed. events.title: Elf (2003)
about: Shown as part of the Williamstown Holiday Walk. Presented for free to the community by the Williamstown Cultural District and Images Cinema.

When young Buddy falls into Santa's gift sack on Christmas Eve, he's transported back to the North Pole and raised as a toy-making elf by Santa's helpers. But as he grows into adulthood, he can't shake the nagging feeling that he doesn't belong. Buddy vows to visit Manhattan and find his real dad, a workaholic publisher.
Directed by Jon Favreau · 1h 37m · PG

events.title: Wild Horse Nine
about: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris and Lee are dispatched from Santiago to Easter Island by their bureau chief, MJ. Directed by Martin McDonagh · 1h 58m · R

events.title: The Green Knight
about: Q&A with costume designer Malgosia Turzanska!
We kick off the holiday season with The Green Knight, David Lowry’s stunning adaptation of the classic Arthurian legend, followed by a conversation with costume designer Malgosia Turzanska!

When the mythical Green Knight (Ralph Ineson) barges into King Arthur’s court on Christmas day, only Arthur’s headstrong nephew Sir Gawain (Dev Patel) accepts his challenge. Forced to face the knight the following Christmas, Gawain sets off on a journey filled with ghosts, giants, thieves, and schemers that tests his character and discover his true strength.

After the screening, we’ll be joined by Academy Award nominated costume designer Malgosia Turzanska to discuss the process of combining historical accuracy and fantasy elements to create the movie’s signature look, and what it took to bring her designs to life.
Directed by David Lowery · 2h 10m · R

events.title: An Evening With - Martin Sexton Live Wide Open Tour
about: Martin Sexton tours in support the 25th anniversary of Live Wide Open - the critically-acclaimed double vinyl live album. The show will include these fan-favorites as well as some new material and surprise covers.

“Mr. Sexton as an impassioned performer can bring women and men to tears when they see him live” —Wall Street Journal “The best live performer I’ve ever seen.” —John Mayer “Master of dynamics, reducing a room to silence with his blustering baritone, then teasing that silence with a fluttering falsetto." —Acoustic Guitar

events.title: Sarah Jarosz: 10 Years of Undercurrent
about: Originally from Wimberley, Texas, Sarah Jarosz is a six-time GRAMMY Award winning singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist. Since her recorded debut in 2009, she has released seven solo albums and two albums with I’m With Her, her band with Sara Watkins and Aoife O’Donovan. In addition to her multiple GRAMMY, Americana Music Association, and Folk Alliance awards, her work has received widespread critical praise from publications including Rolling Stone, The New York Times, and USA Today. Jarosz has appeared three times on PBS’s legendary Austin City Limits television show and numerous times on A Prairie Home Companion, Live From Here, and the Grand Ole Opry. She is currently based in Nashville, Tennessee.

events.title: Crystal Bowersox
events.detail: with Troy Millette & the Fire Below
about: Crystal Bowersox, a northwest Ohio native, has built her world around music. By the age of 10, she was performing in local clubs and venues. On the cusp of 18 and with a curious heart, Crystal moved to Chicago, IL, where she spent her days busking on subway platforms between working odd jobs and attending school.

Chicago’s rich musical history helped Bowersox to broaden her musical horizons. Ultimately, Bowersox auditioned for the ninth season of American Idol, and her time on the show proved to be well spent. In 2010, her debut album, “Farmer’s Daughter” was released on Jive Records and since, she has since released 3 LP’s, two EPs, several singles, and is currently developing a theatrical rock concert titled, "Trauma Queen". Crystal has recorded and performed alongside several notable names and additionally, has used her voice and talents to benefit several organizations close to her heart.

Jeffrey Martin has been reaching for quiet and stories since he was a kid hiding under the covers with a Discman. He wrote his way through a writing degree, a teaching degree, and years of high school English classes filled with unruly brilliance, all while making records and playing shows whenever he could. Eventually, he left teaching to follow the same dream he encouraged his students to chase. After releasing Thank God We Left the Garden, he recorded Alive July 25, 2025, a no-edits live album captured in Portland with Sam Weber. Jeffrey tours full time now, still missing teaching like an old friend he’ll meet again.

"My name is Timothy Steven Corey Parsons (my mom said she couldn’t decide so she named me all of them). A lot of folks call me coco. I was born in Bessemer, AL where Gucci Mane is from but doesn’t claim, got schooled in Hueytown, AL (hence the typos) where Bobby/Davey Allison of NASCAR fame called home, and spent my formative years in Birmingham, AL. I’ve been living in Nashville, TN for a long time. Spent some good times in Austin, TX. And I’ve spent a lot of my life traveling. I was raised by a single mom who worked her ass off to make sure I had a fair shot at life and I hope to one day buy her a Rolls Royce once this music thing takes off. I enjoy writing songs and singing them for people and lucky for me I get to do both of those things quite often. Finishing a song is one of my favorite feelings in the world and I feel it’s important because I…

events.title: An Evening with Eilen Jewell
about: Twenty years of touring. Twenty years on the road. "My own weariness amazes me," as Bob Dylan sings to his Tambourine Man. I feel ya, Bob. But the depth of my gratitude amazes me too. I'm humbled by the countless gifts of fanship and friendship throughout the past two decades. I would say it's been a dream, except I never could have dreamt up most of it. I've shared stages and drinks in hotel rooms with my heroes, met children named after me, made friendships rooted in music from Auckland to the Arctic Circle, performed on trains, on boats, for Wall Street men in tuxes and for the muddy denizens of a musk ox farm... Not bad for a lonely rambler girl from Idaho. It was always a nebulous gut feeling that got the show on the road, and so it is now but in reverse. A gut feeling is telling me to get off the road, at least for now. After 2026, touring and I will part ways for a year, maybe two, maybe fifty...it's hard to say at this point. I do hope to keep performing in some capacity. Maybe come see me of a weeknight in some Boise dive, playing for potatoes? Or strumming the guitar for a handful of fellow meditators as we contemplate the Dharma and the temporary nature of all things. I need some time for a new exploration, to try to be the kind of mother I want to be, and to stop moving long enough "to let my soul catch up with me," as my grandma Jeanne used to say. Who knows what will come of that? Maybe on some jingle-jangle morning I'll come following the next great dream, rested and ready to go anywhere. But until then, suffice it to say...thank you. Thank you, thank you to everyone who carried me forward all this way and in all your different ways. With love, gratitude, and solidarity in music always --Eilen Hailed by American Songwriter as “one of America’s most intriguing, creative, and idiosyncratic voices,” Eilen Jewell rises from the ashes on her captivating new album, Get Behind The Wheel, picking up the pieces of her shattered world and finding new purpose and meaning after watching her marriage, her band, and what felt like her entire career fall apart in a series of spectacular, heartbreaking implosions. Co-produced by multi-instrumental wizard Will Kimbrough (Todd Snider, Hayes Carll), the collection pushes the acclaimed singer and songwriter’s trademark blend of vintage roots-noir into more psychedelic territory, with spacious, cinematic…

about: Twenty years of touring. Twenty years on the road. "My own weariness amazes me," as Bob Dylan sings to his Tambourine Man. I feel ya, Bob. But the depth of my gratitude amazes me too. I'm humbled by the countless gifts of fanship and friendship throughout the past two decades. I would say it's been a dream, except I never could have dreamt up most of it. events.title: AJ Lee & Blue Summit
about: A virtuosic four-piece that’s taken the progressive bluegrass world by storm, AJ Lee & Blue Summit came together as teenagers in the fertile California festival scene, cutting their teeth at campsite jams and parking lot picking sessions before landing their first gigs at bars and cafes around Santa Cruz. After a pair of widely lauded self-released LPs, the group landed a deal with Signature Sounds for their label debut, City Of Glass, which earned rave reviews and led to festival slots everywhere from Telluride and Merlefest to High Sierra and RockyGrass, where their standout set prompted Rolling Stone to declare that “the band can seamlessly weave from bluegrass to country to western swing to folk-rock, with the powerhouse vocals of Lee as the core.”

Cover To Cover, the group’s intoxicating fourth album, taps into the ecstatic energy of the band’s live show, collecting eleven of their favorites covers into a dazzling showcase not only of the band’s superlative musicianship, but also their remarkable ambition and imagination as arrangers and interpreters. Recorded with longtime friend and engineer Jonathan Kirchner and featuring appearances from Jerry Douglas, Lindsay Lou, Skyway Man, and more, the album reinvents tunes by the likes of Sheryl Crow, Bob Dylan, Nitty Gritty Dirt Band, and Emmylou Harris, offering up a fresh perspective on the American roots canon from some of the brightest young torchbearers of their generation.

events.title: Makers Market
about: Makers Market is an invitational craft show featuring contemporary, one-of-a-kind goods and gifts. Shop small this holiday season with handmade, original art and crafts from local artists. New location this year at the Iron Horse Music Hall! Free admission. November 21, Saturday Only, 9-3.

events.title: Willie Nile
about: The New York Times called Buffalo, NY born Willie Nile "one of the most gifted singer-songwriters to emerge from the New York scene in years." Uncut Magazine called him “A one-man Clash.” His album Streets Of New York was hailed as “a platter for the ages” by Uncut. Rolling Stone listed The Innocent Ones as one of the “Top Ten Best Under-The-Radar Albums of 2011” and BBC Radio called it “THE rock ‘n’ roll album of the year.” His single from that album, “One Guitar,” was the “Top Pick of the Week” in USA Today.

Willie has toured across the U.S. with The Who and has sung with Bruce Springsteen and The E Street Band. As the induction program from the Buffalo Music Hall of Fame says: “His live performances are legendary.” His 2020 album New York At Night got rave reviews, with Downbeat calling it a “sonic love letter to Gotham.”

His new studio album The Day The Earth Stood Still features a duet with Steve Earle on the song “Blood On Your Hands.” While many of us have struggled to salvage a sense of purpose from a year’s worth of isolation, Willie tapped into his own lockdown experience as a source of inspiration for the set of haunting new songs that comprise his emotion-charged new album. Although the singer-songwriter borrowed its title from the beloved 1951 science fiction movie classic, the album was inspired by the sight of Nile’s beloved hometown temporarily turned into a desolate ghost town.

“A man who embodies the true spirit of rock n’ roll.” - London Times Dan Zukergood has been a mainstay in the Pioneer Valley music scene for the past 30 years. Many people know him as a member of Johnny and the Flashbacks, Dan Zukergood and the Mostly Happy Band and The Meanies.

Dan has two albums of original material - Mostly Happy Man and I Ain’t Dead Yet! Dan writes heartfelt love songs, songs that reflect his positive attitude towards life, highly political songs and songs that are just plain funny! But no matter what he is writing about, he sure knows how to tell a good story. He is also a huge Willie Nile fan!
This show will be very special as it will be the first time that The Meanies and The Mostly Happy Band (Jim Henry and JJ O’Connell) will be joining forces! It should be a great time!

events.title: Funk Night: Funksgiving
events.detail: with Beau Sasser, Jerry Cortez, Pete Antunes and Nate Fuller
about: GET YOUR FUNK NIGHT MERCH BEFORE THE SHOW SHOP FUNK NIGHT HERE🪩🎶 SHOW: 8:30pm / DOORS: 8:00pm Beau Sasser - Keys Featuring Jerry Cortez and Pete Antunes of Tower of Power Nate Fuller of Sax and Stache Beau Sasser has been a staple artist in the live music scene for decades. He is currently active throughout the Northeast and all over the country with the progressive funk/fusion band Kung Fu, the explosive Frank Zappa tribute band The Z3, the legendary New Orleans-grown Glen David Andrews Band, along with his own projects Escape Plan and Beau Sasser Trio - all of which allow his creative prowess over the keys and organ to shine.

Beau launched Funk Night in Northampton 18 years ago, and after taking the show on the road both far and wide, he's eager to bring his group of show-stopping friends along for the ride at the famed Iron Horse.

events.title: LuxDeluxe
about: The first thing you’ll notice about LuxDexlue is the singer, Ned King. He might be high-kicking, rolling on the floor, or squeezed up alongside drummer Jake Edwards with his own set of sticks in hand. Bassist Jacob Rosazza and rhythm guitarist Jake Manzi lean into their mics as Ned does, and 3-part Eagles-esque harmonies roll out. Then the energy shifts to stage left, where lead guitarist Caleb Rosazza has started soloing, and you know you’re in for a good night.

LuxDeluxe began in a poster-plastered basement in Northampton, Massachusetts in 2009. Three young cousins and two friends got together to play rock & roll, surrounded by stacks of records that included NRBQ, JJ Cale, and Tom Petty. The band rapidly gained recognition for their high-octane shows that left audiences sweaty and earned them the opportunity to share stages with Deer Tick, White Denim, Reptar, Lake Street Dive, Rubblebucket, J Mascis, NRBQ, and Big Al Anderson.

After a decade of writing, recording, and touring, a founding member of the band moved to LA to pursue film work. The pandemic closely followed. Like many bands during the events of 2020, LuxDeluxe went through a quiet period, during which they slowly built up a recording studio in an old warehouse building, and amassed a hoard of vintage guitars, keyboards, and amps. As guitarist Caleb Rosazza built up his inventory of recording gear, the rest of the band dug into honing their own skills, playing with other Western Mass bands, co-writing, and recording for other projects.

In 2022, the band re-convened to write and record over 100 songs, working and re-working to find their sound and identity again. And when they found themselves on stage for 2 sold-out New Year’s shows with NRBQ in 2023, something fell into place.

Their first new music in 7 years will be released in Fall 2024. This will be the band’s 6th release and 4th full-length album in the 15 years they have been together. The joy is still there. Evidence of time passing is, too. These aren’t the songs of kids barely out of high school any more. These songs bind the past to the present: the music may have evolved, but the heart and guts that make a LuxDeluxe record what it is shine through.

events.title: Ronnie Earl & The Broadcasters
about: Legendary Blues guitarist Ronnie Earl is a four-time Blues Music Award winner as Guitar Player of the Year (1997, 1999, 2014, 2018), most recently receiving the award on May 10, 2018, in Memphis. He has served as an Associate Professor of Guitar at Berklee College of Music and has taught at the National Guitar summer workshop in Connecticut.

In 1995 Ronnie released Ronnie Earl: Blues Guitar with Soul, an instructional VHS tape re-released in DVD format in 2005. Earl’s discography includes acclaimed albums on Stony Plain Records, Black Top, Bullseye Blues, Verve, and Telarc. His 1996 Bullseye Blues release, Grateful Heart: Blues and Ballads, won Downbeat Magazine’s Blues Album of the Year, and in 2004 Earl’s Hey José won the Best Blues/R&B Song at the 3rd Annual Independent Music Awards. In 2022, Ronnie Earl and the Broadcasters celebrate 35 years as a band. The recent releases by Ronnie Earl and the Broadcasters, Spread the Love (2010), Just for Today (2013), and Good News (2014), Father’s Day (2015), Maxwell Street (2016), and The Luckiest Man (2017), Beyond The Blue Door (2019) and Rise Up (2020) all debuted on the top ten Billboard Blues charts and received wide critical acclaim. Mercy Me (2022) is Earl’s 14th album in partnership with Stony Plain and his 28th career album.

events.title: Roomful of Blues
about: Roomful of Blues, the world-renowned, horn-powered, houserocking blues band, has been delighting audiences for over 55 years. Blues Music Magazine calls them “the best little big band in the blues.” On record and on stage, Roomful of Blues—led by master guitarist Chris Vachon for the past 25 years—continues to deliver its bone-shaking mix of original songs and carefully chosen covers ranging from jump, swing and proto rock ‘n’ roll to funky, contemporary blues. Their impeccable musicianship and larger-than-life vocals have earned Roomful of Blues five GRAMMY Award nominations and a slew of other accolades, including seven Blues Music Awards. Twice, the prestigious DownBeat International Critics’ Poll has selected them as Best Blues Band. And now, even after 18 previous releases and thousands of live shows, Roomful of Blues continues to evolve. Roomful of Blues, according to DownBeat magazine, “are in a class by themselves.” With their masterful combination of jumping, horn-heavy, hard-edged blues and R&B, it’s no wonder why the great Count Basie called them “the hottest blues band I’ve ever heard.” With a non-stop performance schedule for over 55 years, Roomful of Blues has earned critical, popular and radio success and a legion of fans around the globe. Roomful of Blues guitarist and bandleader Chris Vachon first joined in 1990 and has been leading the band since 1998. Guitar Player says Vachon’s guitar playing “burns with explosive solos and a delightfully greasy sense of rhythm.” The band has maintained its signature sound through great musicianship and a stellar horn section— featuring tenor and alto saxophonist Rich Lataille, who first joined the band in 1970. Lataille’s masterful playing can evoke either the fat-toned, honking sax of the glory days of early rock or the cool elegance of big band swing jazz.

Along with Vachon and Lataille, Roomful of Blues now includes new lead vocalist D.D. Bastos, new keyboardist Jeff Ceasrine, baritone and tenor saxophonist Craig Thomas, trumpeter Christopher Pratt, bassist Lou Bocciarelli and drummer Mike Coffey. The band has never sounded fresher or stronger, with Bastos bringing her sweet and soulful vocals and adding another bright new dimension to Roomful of Blues’ jazzy, jump-blues musical roots. Their winning combination of jump, swing, blues, R&B and soul remains their calling card, as does their ability to…

events.title: Willie Watson
about: Soon before Willie Watson turned 18, he met God in an apple orchard. Or at the very least, he met there a man named Ruby Love, the older friend of a high-school buddy who had an enormous Martin guitar and a seemingly bigger understanding of the American folk songbook. Watson was existentially thirsty: A high-school dropout from upstate New York’s Finger Lakes, he was fast on his way to his first heartbreak and in a first band that didn’t take itself seriously enough. But that night in an apple orchard that had always seemed magical, at a graduation party for one of his bandmates and best friends, Watson and Love sang a few of those old songs together—“Worried Man Blues” and “Tennessee Waltz.” It was the first time Watson had cried while singing, the first time he had made the connection between making music and making sense of his life. He never saw Ruby Love again, but within months of that foundational 1997 rendezvous, he met the musicians with whom he’d soon start Old Crow Medicine Show. Call it revelation, fate, resurrection, whatever you will; for Watson, more than a quarter-century later, it was a duet with the divine.

As told in the talking-gospel masterpiece “Reap ’em in the Valley,” that scene is the transfixing finale of Watson’s self-titled debut as a songwriter and as a human at last making music to make sense of his life. Yes, Watson has released two albums since he left Old Crow Medicine Show a dozen years ago and since his long-term collaborations with David Rawlings and Gillian Welch. But those records, both titled Folk Singer, were sets of tunes he knew, interpretations of the songbook he has diligently mined since even before that night in the apple orchard. At 44, however, he feels that Willie Watson is his first-ever true album, having finally lived and lost and simply witnessed enough to know he has something to sing with his exquisite rural tenor. Watson has not abandoned those old songs entirely. He dazzles during a robust take on the forever-curious “Mole in the Ground” and treats “Harris and the Mare,” the standard of tragic Canadian singer Stan Rogers, with total tenderness. But by and large, these are his stories of heartbreak and hurt, backlit by the corona of hope that only growth can provide.
Every memory, Watson likes to say, is surrounded by a shroud of sadness, whether it’s good or bad. And there are lots of memories in a…

events.title: Chris Smither
about: Born in Miami, during World War II, Chris Smither grew up in New Orleans where he first started playing music as a child. The son of a Tulane University professor, he was taught the rudiments of instrumentation by his uncle on his mother’s ukulele. “Uncle Howard,” Smither says, “showed me that if you knew three chords, you could play a lot of the songs you heard on the radio. And if you knew four chords, you could pretty much rule the world.” With that bit of knowledge under his belt, he was hooked. “I’d loved acoustic music – specifically the blues – ever since I first heard Lightnin’ Hopkins’ Blues In My Bottle album. I couldn’t believe the sound Hopkins got. At first I thought it was two guys playing guitar. My style, to a degree, came out of trying to imitate that sound I heard.”

In his early twenties, Smither turned his back on his anthropology studies and headed to Boston at the urging of legendary folk singer Eric von Schmidt. It was the mid-’60s and acoustic music thrived in the streets and coffeehouses there. Smither forged lifelong friendships with many musicians, including Bonnie Raitt who went on to record his songs, “Love You Like A Man” and “I Feel the Same. (Their friendship has endured as their career paths intertwined over the years.) What quickly evolved from his New Orleans and Cambridge musical experiences is his enduring, singular guitar sound – a beat-driven finger-picking, strongly influenced by the playing of Mississippi John Hurt and Lightnin’ Hopkins, layered over the ever-present backbeat of his rhythmic, tapping feet (always mic’d in performance).

Smither’s first albums, I’m A Stranger, Too! (1971) and Don’t It Drag On (1972) were released on Poppy Records, home of kindred spirit Townes Van Zandt. By the time Smither recorded his third album, Honeysuckle Dog with Lowell George and Dr. John helping out, United Artists had absorbed Poppy and ultimately dropped much of their roster, including Smither. Smither made his next record in 1985, when the spare It Ain’t Easy on Adelphi Records marked his return to the studio.

By the early ’90s, Smither’s steady nationwide touring and regular release of consistently acclaimed albums cemented his reputation as one of the finest acoustic musicians in the country. His 1991 album, Another Way to Find You, was recorded live in front of an in-studio audience with no overdubs or second takes. This…
